DANIELLE: What the hell did you do?
After Zero mentioned we weren't getting any readings, I heard you went off to the other meteor site and then all of a sudden we've got like four new reports and also our equipment busted.
Like it wasn't picking anything up until you got that Giratina, and then all of the energy it should've been detecting came through at once and overloaded it.
So nice going.
Doubt we're going to have any luck finding more Anomalies after the current round unless we can get that repaired.
Anyway, one of the reports we suddenly picked up was super high-speed.
No idea where it came from, but it shot halfway across the region in a blink and currently it's stalled out atop Charous Mountain.
Easiest access is from the Pokémon League.
Hardy already went up there, but I'm pretty sure he permanently forgot his brain cells at home, so you might wanna go help out.

Welcome to the Nightclub's Battle Facilities.
The Battle Pavilion is a traditional Battle Tower style challenge using your own Pokémon,
Whereas in the Battle Factory challenge you instead fight with a selection of randomly rented Pokémon.
The Battle Palace challenge is similar to the Battle Pavilion, however, there's a twist: Your Pokémon will choose their actions themselves!
In addition to this, random Field Effects may be optionally generated before each battle.
Completing a 5 battle round in either challenge with Field Effects enabled will increase your BP reward.

You'll get one random field effect per battle.

ZERO: ...Hey there, \PN.
Surprised to see me out from behind the desk now?
We'd finally finished cleaning up all the Anomaly reports, and, well, uhh...
Figured I'd stick around for a little bit.
Take a little bit of time to relax.
...You know, uh... enjoy the scenery and all.
It can be... a little overwhelming here.
But whether I'm behind the counter managing reports or not...
It's been nice to see everyone back again.
ZERO: ...Thanks for stopping by to say hi.
It's good to see you as always, too.
ZERO: Honestly, \PN, it feels all too weird now.
No reports to manage, no equipment to monitor, no Anomalies to help with...
...No nights losing sleep over how many we received at once sometimes, either.
One part of me kinda thought the reports would never end.
...The other part is sad they're over and done with.
...Heh.
I won't lie, though, it's still been nice to be able to rest at the end of it all.
Seeing everyone here...
Ace, Blake... Cal--
Ace, Taka--
Eve and Lumi, too...
...I, uh... I missed them.
Maybe I could try and talk with them sometime, too.
...Dunno if they'd want to, but...
Might be nice.
ZERO: You know, \PN, I've been thinking.
I kinda want to see if there's other places where I can try and help out, too.
Between helping manage the Anomaly reports, and that, uh, freezing New World expedition together...
It was... a lot to manage.
But it just... felt right.
To finally be able to do something right myself.
Being able to support you there, and support behind the counter here...
ZERO: ...Y'know, \PN...
All that time behind the desk got me thinking.
Kinda want to see if there's some other places where I can try and help out, too.
Helping manage all of those Anomaly reports...
It just... felt right.
If we could all do the little things within our power to help the people around us, then maybe things wouldn't be so bad.
...U-uh, sorry to lay that on you suddenly.
You know, again.
Thanks for hearing me out, though.
ZERO: Heh, guess I've gotta figure out what else to do nowadays, huh.
It's uh, weird to not have anything to do.
...Don't have to tell me twice how much I've been blabbering about it.
I'm just glad that there's even been something that someone like me could do for this whole clusterfuck.
ZERO: ...Uh.
"Someone like me" is only rude to myself, I guess.
This is... embarrassing, but sometimes it still helps me to think of myself as if I were still different people.
I wouldn't want to talk like that to Eve and Lumi.
I know they wouldn't say that to me.
So, uh... to correct it...
I'm proud that I could still make a difference here.
Help around with fighting the good fight.
ZERO: I'm glad you stopped by for a chat over here.
...Maybe I'll join everyone sometime.
ZERO: Need any kind of support today?
...Or were you just saying hi?
ZERO: It can be kind of disorienting here sometimes.
Not that I mind, though.
Good music, people who... still tolerate me? Friends?
It's nice.

Unlike a certain someone's Palace in a certain tropical region, in our Palace, Pokémon can actually fight at their full potential!
I'm not sure if the Pokémon in Reborn are smarter or what, but here, they'll actually fight kinda competently! No more indecision or bad moves!
And, here, they even know when to return to their Poké Ball and let their teammates do the fighting!
You don't have to do anything! So, that said...

ARC: Hey. \PN, right? Come over here.
ARC: You remember me? From the Nightclub.
Look, I've been keeping my eye on this place for a while. There's something fishy about it, yanno.
And I've seen you buy from this guy a few times, yeah? But you don't seem like his typical customer to me.
???: Hey, you. Come here.
Who are you? I've been keeping my eye on this place for a while, but you don't seem like this guy's typical customer to me.
\PN, huh?
Well, I'm Arclight- DJ Arclight, to be specific. I run the Nightclub up in the Obsidia Ward.
You can just call me Arc. Anyway.
I'm pretty sure that these Pokémon he's selling are stolen, and I ain't about that.
Most of his customers don't care a thing about Pokémon. They usually end up abusing them.
If these Pokémon really are stolen, it's probably hopeless to find their original owners, but, I figure at least we can get them to a good place.
And I'm thinkin' you might be that good place.
So I'll tell you what, \PN, I'm gonna leave it to you to buy up the rest of these guys. He won't sell to me; I've raised hell here in the past.
And once we've cleaned his stock, then I'll bust in and clean his clock.
Make sure this guy gets shut down for good. Sound like a plan?
I'm countin' on you.
ARC: Yo. \PN.
If these Pokémon really are stolen, it might not be practical to find their original owners, but, I figure at least we can get them to a good place.
Huh, you already did it? Not bad.
Looks like you did it, huh?
I owe you one, for sure. I can rest a bit easier knowing that those Pokémon will be taken care of no matter what.
It might not be a bad idea to hang onto them just in case though.
As for that guy... I won't do anything out in the open.  But let me put it this way-- Next time you're around here, don't expect to see him again.
Anyway, here's a little 'thank you' from me.
Do what you will with that.
If you ever get into the Nightclub, hit me up for sure!
CRAUDBURRY: Miserable lout, PATHETIC inventory, if this is really all you've got, you ought to be ashamed of your scruffy-rumped self!
Don't call again until you have something worth my time!
CRAUDBURRY: Oh, it's you.
I shoulda known I'd see low-life scum like you lollygagging around down here.
Don't look at me, criminal swine, you aren't worth my breath! Drivelling mucus with every step... Bah!
ARCHER: Quite the mouth that one has, doesn't she?
MAXWELL: You gonna let her talk to you like that?
ARCHER: Perhaps unfortunately, the street-savvy aren't the only ones with influence down here.
There's always people like Craudburry. She pretends to be such an upstanding citizen, but she just plays the streets down here with her wealth.
You recall the Pokémon we stole from her, yes? That was one she purchased illegally down here.
That's why I had no regrets in targeting her.
Nonetheless, her attitude is insufferable. Yet, no one down here stands up to her.
After all, they dare not risk her patronage.
I'm thinking, though, perhaps we might better everyone's lives down here if we, how do you say, teach her a lesson?
If you're interested, find me around her house.
MAXWELL: I'll tell you what, that broad has way too much power down here.
This is supposed to be place for the strong to survive, not for some rich bitch to order everyone around as she pleases.
But that's just it. Money casts a powerful curse. And she gets what she wants.
Like stolen Pokémon. You know?
That's why I tried to take it back from her before. She didn't even play fair to get it.
Most people don't dare stand up to someone like her-- they might lose their squeeze.
But us? We're different.
Know what I mean? I think we oughta teach that one a lesson.
Come find me around her house. We'll settle this score.
For, you know, glory.
DEFACTO: Well met, \PN.
Do tell, how do you find business down here?
Personally, I manage to make a pretty penny, but it can be a veritable struggle to reason with some of these lesser merchants.
See, the economy down here-- as with any underworld market-- works on a separate axis of supply and demand.
One singular substance reigns supreme here: "Rare Candy". Heard of it?
Well, perhaps it is best that someone like you never does. For many of these fellows, however, they are already too addicted to the "level up".
Incidentally, do you know how "Rare Candy" is made?
By distilling the synthetic compounds of other items-- specifically Crystal Shards and Heart Scales-- one is left with a highly reactive substance.
Combined with the traditional medicinal Pokémon Rare Candy, a violent psychoactive is produced.
But, as such, it is these ingredients which are in high demand down here: Shards and Heart Scales.
Thus, it is extremely beneficial for those able to gather these resources to do so.
This is where I come in!
I have a brand new product that can help the crafty geologist maximize their efficiency.
Blast Powder is a unique reactive substance.
When placed on certain kinds of damaged rock-- the glowing sediment I'm sure you've seen-- it will allow previously harvested spots to become lucrative.
In short, it allows you to mine a stone twice.
That established... Buy some!
DEFACTO: You return! Come to buy more Blast Powder?
BREAK: Oh, \PN! Do stay a moment, I have an amazing discovery to regale you with!
Although this is 7th Street, some find it more like a 7th Heaven. Do you know why?
Oh, I shall tell you. It's because they're out of their minds!
Literally~
Do tell, do tell, have you ever tried "Rare Candy"?
Oh, I suspect you haven't-- it's not what you feed your Pokémon.
This is a very special kind of "level up".
But I will tell you the ingredients of the thing!
SUGAR!
SPICE!
And EVERYTHING NICE!
Just kidding.
Actually it's the benzoylmethylecgonine dust and crystal-isomerized piperonyl acetone embedded in Heart Scales and crystal Shards.
Then you stick that in a normal Rare Candy and you'll be partyin' it up, down, sideways AND diagonally.
Anyway, it turns out Heart Scales and Shards are useful to collect.
Not always easy though! They play hard to get.
By hiding in hard things, like rocks.
Sure, you can mine some out, but then what?
I'll tell you what! Then you take some Blast Powder and blow up the base of the rock so you can mine even MORE out!
Then you sell them and become king of the world! Or queen. Or whatever.
Anyway yes, Blast Powder! Mine things twice! Buy some!
BREAK: Blast Powder! More fun than exploding chocolate cake!
Merry mining~!
DEFACTO: You're back at last!
Might I interest you in a fresh stock of Blast Powder?
Oh, please refrain from invoking any of that platitudinous job-seeking discourse that the boss has been so intent on spouting off.
As his analytical holiness refuses to acknowledge, I am already gainfully employed right here.
As such, why not indulge yourself?
DEFACTO: Admittedly, it might have been a boon to be in a slightly more intellectual line of work.
Knowledge is the seat of personal growth, but aside from which downcast countenaces are the most likely customers, there's little to be learned here.
But that anything like that would exist in this city is a far cry. I'm content here.
BREAK: \PN! My old friend and most valued customer~!
Listen! We've got a problemo in the gang and his name is Maxwell.
But the way he's talking about breaking us up, we oughta call him Maxunwell!
Ohoh, don't look at me like that. It's spine-tingling.
More seriously, I can't think of a job better suited to my talents than synthesizing benzoylmethylecgonine.
Most people can't even pronounce that word.
It's a gift.
I suppose I am familiar with a variety of chemical, herbal and questionably legal substances that might be handy to those with bizarre interests...
But really, no one these days likes to think outside the box.
So we might as well just blow stuff up!
Remember, if it doesn't seem like a good idea, that just means you're not using enough sparklers.
You Aqua punks still struttin' around like you're so cool?
Hmph. Not like it matters now.
Please, your blank stare is piercing into my soul. I cannot possibly exist under the pressure of your black-pixel eyes.
Even in its death-- I will show you the true POWER of the Magma Gang!
You are strong indeed.
Hoo-hah. I bow to a strength greater than my own.
I'm not letting the Aqua Gang go down without a fight!
Too strong.
Man, how many Rare Candies did you feed YOUR Pokémon? All of mine weren't enough!
Send out your Pokémon.
You have no need to speak to me.
Oh, man. I like what I'm seein'. You? You look like fresh meat.
Ugh, I was the one who got chewed up and spit out.
Lesson learned, don't judge the book by its cover.
Dude... The Butterfree are soooo like lackadaisical. They totally just morphed into that beam...
Aha, yah, wha? What's going on?
Duuuuuuude...
Dude. I'm sooo fuckin' leveled right now. Fight me!
Woaaaaah...
Like, shit. Shiiiiiit.
Dude. You new around here? I don't think I seen you before.
LOL, I'm just messin' with you man. How are you?!
It's been a while! Man, remember last time we dropped Candy together?
...Wait, you mean you really don't know me?
Shit dude, you're not with them, are you?
I don't trust you. I never seen you around here before.
You're obviously a cop in disguise! Get away from me!
I don't know why my boyfriend insists on selling down here all the time.
All these men are so creepy.
Bro, you got any "Rare Candy" to spare?
Heh... 'Spare Candy'. That's good.
Hey, you got a problem, bud?!
You think I steal from you? I ain't steal from you!
If you gotta problem, let's go! You wanna go?!
Fuck, dude.
What the hell, dude. You can have your shit back, christ.
Fuck me, you looked like an easy pick, too... Dammit.
Stow it, I'll leave you alone.
Dude, you wanna give me some cash? I need a fix...
Some people was worried that the fuzz would bust this place up if it was found during the construction.
Hah! We show 'em.
Incompetent police don't have a clue!
7th Street is the one place that won't change! This is OUR world!
NIHIL: Sup.
I see you took your time in making it down here.
This has been our squeeze for quite some time.
Surprised I didn't see you 'round before.
Hm, you're looking for someone?
I mean, I'm right here.
Chill, it was a joke.
I saw someone suspicious run into the watering hole just a minute ago.
Go get 'im, tiger.
NIHIL: Dude, any guy who runs from you isn't worth your time.
NIHIL: You wanna talk about the job thing, right?
Yeah, forget it.
There's no way I'm stooping that low.
Do whatever you want with the other guys, but there's not a job in this city worthy of me.
Wherever I worked would have to be the last word in cool.
And this is Reborn City.
They don't do cool.
DARM: BRO! You here to get pumped up?
This place has the best "level-ups"!
Whaddya mean you aren't here for that?
Everyone's here for that.
That shit is POWERFUL.
Oh, huh. You're lookin' for someone?
Well, I dunno about a girl, but I just saw some weird guy headin' up to the watering hole.
You could probably catch him if you hurry.
DARM: Magma is strength!
DARM: BRO! We gotta get jobs?!
That's BALLS.
But if everyone else is doing it, I guess I got to.
All right-- I want the kinda job that I can get POWERFUL on.
I gotta get people to praise me like "YO how that dude so swole?!"
I don't have any qualifications besides my rippling pecs and bulging biceps.
And not even construction crews would take me. I break stuff, not make stuff!
So what's there left to do but be the muscle in the city streets, huh?!
If Maxwell's backing down from leading the Magma Gang, I'll do it in his stead!
PIERCE: How about it, then?
...Looking for someone?
Check the watering hole, right there.
PIERCE: ...Hm.
So we're getting jobs.
To tell the truth,
I don't think I can do that.
I don't like talking to people.
I never know what to say.
Most jobs make you deal with things like customers, or a boss who can fire you at any time...
I... can't do that.
If I could, I'd just want to go somewhere quiet.
I don't have to talk. I don't have to work.
Just let me be in peace.
RAZZY: Hey! What's up! You gettin' hype on the "level-ups"?
Huh, why not?
Ohhh, you came here looking for someone.
You'll totally find her! You can do anything!
Actually, waitasecond...
I didn't see a girl, but there was this weird guy wanderin' around a moment ago.
I think he was going up towards the watering hole.
Y'wanna see if you can catch him?
RAZZY: Aqua Gang can accomplish anything together!
RAZZY: Together, we can fix this city-- or break it!
RAZZY: So Archer wants us to split up and get jobs...
Okay! I can dig it!
I've never worked before, and I couldn't begin to guess how to write a resume, but I'll do my best!
But what kind of place should I work?
Mmm, I wanna work somewhere that's really upbeat and exciting!
And it should have lots of good food!
Also, I hope it's nearby!
I still live with my parents, and it's not like they'd let me go out of the city for work.
Plus, if it's a short walk, that's even easier for me!
Wait, does something that convenient even exist?
You a new face around here? Scram!
Uh, aite. Go in peace, or whatever.
Mate, 'm not here looking for trouble. Leave me be, aight?
